chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man dies and leaves sons, the eldest is entitled to the sword, the armor, the ring, and the Quran. If an event (death) befalls him, then it is for the eldest among them.
ai.seo_question: What special items does the eldest son inherit according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'fayd' (special inheritance) for the eldest son, granting him exclusive rights to the father's sword, armor, ring, and Quran, reflecting the patriarchal and martial status of the father in early Shia jurisprudence. The conditional clause ensures that if the eldest son predeceases the distribution, the right passes to the next eldest, maintaining the primogeniture rule for these specific honorific items. This ruling is often discussed in contrast to the general division of wealth among all heirs, highlighting the symbolic value of these artifacts in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man dies, and he leaves sons. So, for the eldest is the sword, and the armour, and the ring, and the Parchment. So if there befalls with him what befalls (death), so it is for the eldest among them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When a man dies and leaves behind sons, the eldest son receives the sword, coat of arms, the ring and his (holy) book. If something happens to him then such items belong to the eldest son.’”
